stem: Input solution EC remains stable, but root-zone EC rises during a period of much deeper dryback. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Assume the fertilizer concentrate changed composition even though input EC is stable, because concentrate chemistry can shift without affecting conductivity
Assume crop water uptake has stopped because a rising root-zone EC during deeper dryback indicates ions are accumulating while water remains unchanged
Lower root-zone water content can concentrate dissolved ions, so nutrition and irrigation data should be interpreted together
Treat the EC increase as evidence of a micronutrient shortage because deeper dryback preferentially concentrates macronutrients and reduces trace-element uptake
rationale: Root-zone concentration depends on both dissolved ions and water content. Deeper dryback can increase measured EC even when the incoming solution has not changed.
